[1] Space Lua/JavaScript Interop.md (Accessing browser APIs)
  Converting between Lua and JavaScript values: Lua tables and JavaScript objects/arrays are different types. Space Lua converts between them automatically where possible. Use these functions when you need an explicit conversion: / * `js.tojs(luaValue)` — converts a Lua value to its JavaScript equivalent / * `js.tolua(jsValue)` — converts a JavaScript value to its Lua equivalent
  - Space Lua converts between Lua tables and JavaScript objects/arrays automatically where possible.
[2] MCP.md (Tools)
  Tools: Every client sees the same tools on every space: / * `help`: the first call. Lists the spaces you can use, whether each has a runtime, and the skills available. Tools take a space by its name or its id, the id is needed only when two of your spaces share a name. / * `read`, `write` and `edit`: read pages (a part of one, several at once, or rendered with queries evaluated and lint problems listed), write whole pages, or make targeted edits. Writing a page with Space Lua or Space Style reloads it and reports any load errors. / * `search`: full-text (and, where enabled, semantic) [[Search]] over a space. / * `lua`: run [[Space Lua]] in the live space, with the result and console output. Needs the [[Runtime API]].

  - API reference for the Lua `space` object, listing the functions that read, write, list, delete, lint and version pages, documents and files in a space. Names: space, Git, Lua, space-lua, YAML, X-Ray.
[5] Object Index.md (Indexing)
  - The Object Index is generally queried using Space Lua/Integrated Query.
[6] Migrate from v1.md (Queries)
  - The `config.set` Space Lua API can be used in any Space Lua block.
  Queries: v2 does not have support for old-style [queries](https://v1.silverbullet.md/Query%20Language) (live queries) anymore. They have been replaced with [[Space Lua/Integrated Query]]. Give the linked page a read, but generally there’s a few differences: / 1. Space Lua Integrated Queries tend to start with `from index.objects("tag-name")` instead of plain `tag-name`. This is a bit longer, but since whatever comes after `from` is a Lua expression, you can not just query [[Object]], you can query any Lua table as well in the same way. / 2. In the old query language, you access attribute simply by their name, this works in SLIQ too, but stylistically it’s nicer to use either `_.attribute`, or to give the object you’re iterating over a name, using `from page = index.pages()`, for instance. / 3. The `=` equals operator is `==` in Lua 😄
Exact facts:
- [1] Space Lua runs in the browser and has direct access to JavaScript APIs through the `js` module. This enables you to use the browser’s native capabilities and import external JavaScript libraries. Imported code runs with the same browser access as your Space Lua.
- [1] Space Lua handles JavaScript promises transparently. When a JavaScript function returns a Promise, Space Lua automatically awaits it — you don’t need to write any special async/await code:
- [1] See also: [[API/js]], [[Space Lua]]
